note: A loudly-named test bed for ICM | Calculate Credits, seeded on tool prod because
that is the only environment where Plan, Rule, Transaction and the org data all
exist together. Everything is prefixed TEST- and carries batchId TEST-CC-01, so
the whole family is findable and removable by hand.
WHY ITS OWN SEATS AND PEOPLE. The engine resolves a payee NAME to the seat that
person held on the transaction date. Against the live org data that resolution is
unusable: Priya Nair, Diane Whitlock and Liam Patel each hold TWO live seats in
September 2026, and every seat carrying T-AE in that month is either contested or
vacant. A test bed that cannot produce a single clean credit proves nothing, so
this set stands up four seats of its own rather than editing anybody's data.
WHAT EACH LANE PROVES. Two plans reach these seats and only one may win each deal:
TEST-POS-AE-01  no plan on the seat  -> falls through to the TITLE plan
(TEST-PLAN-SMOKE-01 on T-AE) -> TEST-CR-SMOKE-01, NEW_BOOKING,
splitBps 10000 which OVERRIDES the row's own 70%, rollup 2 levels
TEST-POS-AE-02  TEST-PLAN-SEAT-01 assigned to the SEAT -> wins over the title
plan even though the seat also carries T-AE. TEST-CR-SEAT-01 has
no splitBps, so the ROW's split stands. No rollup.
The two rules file under different credit types on purpose: the creditType on the
credit is what says which lane won, and a demo where both lanes look alike proves
precedence for neither.
THE EIGHT TRANSACTIONS ARE FOUR POSITIVE AND FOUR NEGATIVE. A run that credits all
eight is as wrong as one that credits none, and only the negatives tell them apart.
C01  seat lane, 100%                    -> RENEWAL 5,934.84
C02  title lane, row 70% but rule 100%  -> NEW_BOOKING 5,934.84 + 2 rolled
C03  seat lane, row 70% and no override -> RENEWAL 1,750.00  (proves source split)
C04  billing credit, NEGATIVE amount    -> RENEWAL -268.82   (must NOT be dropped)
C05  incentive date in June             -> never fetched; the window filter is
server-side, so `scanned` should be 7
C06  payee holds no seat                -> NO_POSITION
C07  a name no Payee carries            -> UNRESOLVED_PAYEE
C08  RSM seat                           -> unmatched, NOT NO_PLAN. See below.
MEASURED on tool, run 6aa2abad3c7f7b6b9111fe38 (dry):
scanned 12 | credits 6 (4 direct + 2 rolled) | unmatched 1 | refused 7 | outOfWindow 0
TWO OF THOSE NUMBERS ARE NOT WHAT THIS SET PREDICTED, and both corrections are the
engine being right rather than the engine being wrong:
scanned is 12, not 7. Five transactions already on tool fall inside SEP-2026 and
carry no payee name at all, so they come back as NO_PAYEE_NAME. That is correct:
a run is scoped to a PERIOD, not to a batch, and every row in the window is its
business. There is deliberately no batchId input - a filter that made a partial
calculation look complete is worth more damage than the noise it would remove.
outOfWindow 0 with scanned 12 also proves the window filter is doing its work
SERVER-side: C05 never came back at all.
C08 does not raise NO_PLAN. TEST-POS-RSM-01 carries T-RSM, and a pre-existing plan
('Testing 3', PLAN-1789032727380-3055) is assigned to that title for 10-24 Sep with
an EMPTY creditRules list. So a plan was found, no rule fired, and the row counted
as unmatched - which is the normal, silent outcome, not an exception. The case
still earns its place: it is now the proof that 'a plan with no rules' and 'no plan
at all' are different answers.
AMOUNTS ARE MINOR UNITS. Transaction.amount and Credit.amount are both `integer`
columns titled 'Amount (minor units)', so 5,934.84 is 593484. The values mirror the
real Salesforce export rows they are named after.
PERIOD. SEP-2026 is OPEN, so a run against it is legal under the period state
machine. Nothing here touches JAN-2026 (PAID) or any CLOSED month.
